text:
elena-sales: Hey team — Zenith Health signed the enterprise term sheet. They want 10k RPS peak for chat embeddings + generation during business hours. Need quick presales checklist for reserve vs burst, and answers for the security questionnaire.

jake-se: Congrats! Do we have traffic profile (p95 qps per minute) or is that 10k sustained?

elena-sales: 10k peak sustained for 2 hours/day, 1.5k baseline otherwise. Burst to 12k for 10m spikes. Latency SLO p95 <= 350ms for short prompts.

maya-ml: Model mix: embedding calls ~40%, gen (chat) ~60%. Gen average tokens 120, context window 2k. We're planning quantized 8-bit for cost.

ben-platform: For Dedicated reserved GPUs — rough thumb: to hit 10k RPS for mixed traffic with quantized gen, we'll need ~8 x A10-equivalent workers with batching/kv warm caches. That's a runway estimate; I'll run synthetic.

olivia-sre: Important: AZ spread and eviction tolerance. If they require 99.9% uptime SLA, we need cross-AZ capacity mirrored or burst credits. Also plan autoscale cooldowns to avoid oscillation on those 10m spikes.

elena-sales: They asked about cost tradeoff of reserved vs burst credits in questionnaire — can someone draft the line items (reserved monthly + burst credits cost)?

ben-platform: I'll post a quick math snippet. For reserved: monthly reserve for 8 GPUs = $Xk/mo (placeholder). Burst credits: $Y per 1k peak-minutes. We'll flesh numbers after synthetic run.

jake-se: Ops questions from the customer: preheat/kv warmup strategy, warmup time, and can we auto-fallback to smaller model if latency breaches?

maya-ml: Warmup: with prefix caching and background KV prime we can warm common user prompts in ~5–10 mins per worker. KV priming script:

```
# kv-prime pseudo
for prompt in top_prompts.txt:
  call /v1/prime?model=redwood-quantized -d "{prompt}"
```

Also we support fallback policies in the routing layer — canary to smaller model automatically.

olivia-sre: Note: Autoscale policy recommendation — keep a baseline pool (1.2x expected sustained demand), scale stepwise with 3m cooldown, and a separate burst lane for short spikes that uses reserved burst slots to avoid cold starts.

elena-sales: Security questionnaire: they asked about KMS, audit logs retention, and private deployment options. Who owns the answers?

ben-platform: I'll draft answers: we integrate with customer KMS, audit logs retention configurable up to 13 months, private VPC option available for enterprise (air-gapped packaged for regulated).

jake-se: Also confirm that dedicated pools can be isolated per-tenant for data locality — yep.

olivia-sre: One operational blocker: if they require AZ affinity (keep sessions in same AZ), that reduces our effective capacity headroom. Call it out.

elena-sales: Good call. Add it to the presales risks section.

ben-platform: Plan of action: I'll run a quick synthetic with our mixed traffic simulator, post expected worker counts and cost delta by EOD. Maya will validate kv-warm and fallback timings. Olivia will propose autoscale + AZ config. Jake/elena to bundle answers into the security questionnaire draft.

deploy-bot: preheat-job-1789 started by ben-platform (kv-prime). Logs: 40 prompts enqueued.

elena-sales: Thanks — if we can get numbers today I can send the questionnaire + capacity appendix to Zenith. :raised_hands:

maya-ml: will validate and ping when done. :white_check_mark:

ben-platform: running simulations now, will post results in this thread with sample cost table.

olivia-sre: Also tagging @eng-oncall for any infra limits we should be aware of before committing reserved GPUs.

jake-se: thumbs up.

elena-sales: all right — syncing 3pm PT to finalize.
